prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application composition, 1536x1024 landscape, orthographic straight-on screenshot, no browser chrome or device frame.
Primary request: Design TrailWeaver’s Incident Investigation Dashboard for a cloud security analyst. It must look like a credible premium enterprise security product, not a student admin dashboard.
Input images: Image 1 is visual reference only for the very slim near-black icon rail, oversized heading, warm rounded application canvas, pill navigation, modular soft cards, and restrained lime. Image 2 is visual reference only for serious operational density, selective charcoal analysis surfaces, and compact relationship/data presentation. Image 3 is visual reference only for a practical light enterprise grid, readable compact metrics, and efficient spacing. Do not copy any reference layout, branding, charts, or content.
Shared visual system: a slim near-black left navigation rail; a warm off-white/light-gray main workspace; card surfaces in soft white and pale gray; charcoal primary type and subtle gray secondary type; soft 1px borders; large but disciplined 14–16px corner radii; precise contemporary grotesk sans; tabular numerals; monospace only for IDs, ARNs, and timestamps. Restrained electric lime/yellow-green appears only in active navigation, selected states, one or two key emphases, and timeline markers. Selective dark charcoal surfaces add investigation focus, never full dark mode. Semantic severity uses labeled restrained red/orange/amber/muted green and never color alone.
Sidebar: small TrailWeaver woven-path mark and wordmark, then only Overview / Incidents, Investigations, Cloud Context, Settings, using icons plus compact labels without overcrowding.
Header text: “Investigating” on the first line and large “Possible AWS Account Compromise” beneath it. Metadata nearby: “INC-7F3A2”, actor “developer”, time range “10:01–10:08 UTC”, and a discreet “API connected” status.
Summary row content: “Risk score 80 / 100 Critical”, “Incident severity High”, “Correlated signals 3”, “Potentially reachable assets 5”. These are context modules, not generic business KPI cards; avoid icon-in-square-card repetition.
Segmented section navigation: Overview selected, Timeline, ATT&CK, Blast Radius, Guidance.
Incident timeline exact content: “10:01 Console login without MFA”, “10:04 New access key created”, “10:08 AdministratorAccess attached”. Communicate progression as a causal evidence sequence, not a generic activity feed.
Risk explanation exact content: “Risk 80 / 100 Critical”, “+20 Login without MFA”, “+20 New access key created”, “+40 AdministratorAccess granted”, plus short note “Deterministic total from observed signals”. No circular gauge.
Observed mapping exact content under “Observed ATT&CK mappings”: “T1078.004 Cloud Accounts”, “T1098.001 Additional Cloud Credentials”, “T1098.003 Additional Cloud Roles”, plus caution “Observed behavior mapping—not proof of intent”.
Blast radius exact content under “Potentially reachable known assets”: “5 assets”, “Storage 2”, “Compute 1”, “Database 1”, “Secret 1”, plus caution “Potential reachability—not observed access”.
Guidance exact titles: “Verify login origin”, “Review new access key activity”, “Validate AdministratorAccess assignment”, “Review potentially reachable resources”. Each has a visible priority label and one concise rationale line.
Future graph: do not draw nodes or edges. Reserve a natural future M17 location by placing an inactive “Graph · M17” sub-tab beside ATT&CK within the observed-behavior module, while ATT&CK remains active.
All data is clearly representative sample incident content, not production claims. No raw CloudTrail JSON.
Avoid: cyberpunk, neon hacker, Matrix, green-on-black terminal look, glowing edges, terminal font everywhere, generic Bootstrap/admin template, huge charts, pie/donut charts, decorative gauges, glassmorphism, excessive gradients, oversized empty cards, nested cards, stock photography, fake SOC metrics, fake attack graph, watermark.
Variant 2 — Risk-explanation-dominant.
Keep the same shell, header, summary facts, and navigation, but make a selective-dark charcoal “Explainable Risk” ledger the dominant upper-left focal module after the header. Show 80 / 100 with Critical as a label, then make the +20, +20, +40 contributions visually additive in a horizontal or stepped evidence ledger so the total is immediately understandable. Place the other incident summary modules in a compact supporting band, not equal generic KPI tiles. Below, make a wide light horizontal “Incident Timeline” progression with the three exact events and a restrained lime connecting line. Place a medium-width light guidance column at right. Fit compact Observed ATT&CK mappings and Potentially reachable known assets beneath the timeline. This should feel like a rigorous case brief whose score provenance is visible immediately.
